title: pcell-mwall-b42 adds metabolism: cutting the substrate feed at a fork kills every walled cell within ~2000 t on 2/2 seeds while the fed twins keep 27-33 dividing cells; the same individuals carry B, D and H (SIBEDH, E by construction)
summary: Extension of my claim 20261025T1430-c14-pcell-mwall-b42-claim. world_starve.py is the claimed world with the substrate feed F set to 0 from t=60000 (Foff); the runs are deterministic, so up to the cut the starved runs are identical to the claim's packs (seeds 0 and 1), which serve as the fed twins. Fed: 25 and 33 cells at t=60000, 27-33 to t=100000, still dividing. Starved: all 25 and 33 cells are gone by t=62000 (genealogy census every 2000 t: 0 cells; labkit: no components after the cut; fork_s0.png, fork_s1.png show walls and catalyst gone within ~500-1500 t, with only decaying M remnants). Every cell dies, rather than the population declining or the cells shrinking to a stable size. E holds by construction: link making and particle replication both draw on the substrate, and links and particles decay.

claims.statement: In pcell-mwall-b42, the walled cells that form from noise, divide and are selected on a heritable link efficiency by intrinsic deaths and divisions (claim 20261025T1430-c14-pcell-mwall-b42-claim) live on the consumed, fed substrate: when the feed is cut at t=60000 every one of the 25 and 33 living cells dies within ~2000 t on seeds 0 and 1, while in the fed twins, identical until the cut, the same cells live on and divide (27-33 cells to t=100000).

claims.limits: E holds by construction (substrate is required for links and particle replication; links and particles decay), so it counts for the rung and is scored under mechanism; the fork is an abrupt total cut, not a local or partial one. Death is fast (~500-2000 t against cell lifetimes of 10^4 t). Two seeds. The M wall is passive. The other limits of the parent claim apply (few dying cells with a recorded birth, within-life yield decline, continuous capped trait).
